subject: Gamma function
hook: GAMMA FUNCTION IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The Gamma function is not the only way to extend the factorial function to non-integers; there are infinitely many "pseudogamma" functions that satisfy the same basic factorial property.
angle_support: The gamma function is not only smooth but analytic... but it is not the only analytic function that extends the factorial, as one may add any analytic function that is zero on the positive integers, such as ksin(mπx) for an integer m.
But this still does not give a unique solution, since it allows for multiplication by any periodic function g(x) with g(x)=g(x+1) and g(0)=1, such as g(x)=eksin(mπx) for any integer m.
title: Infinite Pseudogamma Functions: More Than Just the Gamma
description: Most people think the Gamma function uniquely extends factorials to non‑integers. Mathematics shows you can multiply it by any period‑1 analytic function and still satisfy the factorial recurrence, creating endless alternatives. This reveals a whole family of "pseudogamma" functions.
narration: GAMMA FUNCTION IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You assume the Gamma function is the sole way to extend n! to non‑integers. In fact, countless other functions meet the same factorial rule for all positive x. If g(x) is any period‑1 analytic function with g(0)=1, then f(x)=Γ(x)·g(x) satisfies f(x+1)=x f(x). Examples include g(x)=e^{k sin(mπx)} for any integer m, yielding infinitely many pseudogamma functions such as the Hadamard function on the positive real line. Infinite pseudogamma families prove factorial extension isn’t unique for real arguments.
